slides.heading: Design Fundamentals 1/4
slides.subtitle: Topics 1–6
slides.narration: Design fundamentals, part 1 of 4. We'll cover What are design fundamentals?, Client–server model, Network protocols, Storage, Latency and throughput, and Availability.

slides.heading: 1. What are design fundamentals?
bullets: Four pillars: the basis (networking, storage), the key characteristics (availability, latency, throughput, redundancy, consistency), the components (LBs, caches, proxies, DBs), the tech (Kafka, Redis, S3...)
slides.narration: What are design fundamentals?. Four pillars: the basis (networking, storage), the key characteristics (availability, latency, throughput, redundancy, consistency), the components (LBs, caches, proxies, DBs), the tech (Kafka, Redis, S3 ).

slides.heading: 2. Client–server model
bullets: the client opens a connection to the server's port
slides.narration: Client–server model. DNS resolves to an IP. the client opens a connection to the server's port. the server listens. HTTP runs on 80, HTTPS on 443.

slides.heading: 3. Network protocols
bullets: IP packets, TCP (ordered, reliable, handshake), UDP (fast, lossy), HTTP request/response on top of TCP
slides.narration: Network protocols. IP packets, TCP (ordered, reliable, handshake), UDP (fast, lossy), HTTP request or response on top of TCP.

slides.heading: 4. Storage
bullets: databases are just servers that write to disk
slides.narration: Storage. Memory versus disk. persistence. databases are just servers that write to disk.

slides.heading: 5. Latency and throughput
bullets: Latency = time per operation (memory ~µs, SSD ~100 µs, cross-continent ~150 ms)
slides.narration: Latency and throughput. Latency equals time per operation (memory about µs, SSD about 100 µs, cross-continent about 150 ms). Throughput equals operations per second. Improve them separately.

slides.heading: 6. Availability
bullets: Redundancy, no single point of failure, passive/active failover
slides.narration: Availability. Nines (99.99 percent about 52 min a year). SLA versus SLO. Redundancy, no single point of failure, passive or active failover.

slides.heading: Recap
slides.narration: To recap this part: What are design fundamentals?; Client–server model; Network protocols; Storage; Latency and throughput; Availability. Each of these shows up again in the design walkthroughs.
